courses.title: Builder Gel Overlay and Short Extension CPD Course
courses.accredited_title: Builder Gel Overlay and Short Extension CPD Course
courses.short: Add builder gel overlays and short extensions to your services. A one-day classroom course for qualified nail professionals, with online pre-course study, assessed by a theory paper, an observed practical and three case studies.
courses.description: A practical skills-development course for existing beauty and nail professionals. You will revisit nail anatomy and the conditions that mean a service must be adapted, postponed or refused; understand how gel cures, why builder gel carries a heat-spike risk that gel polish does not, and how to control it; and learn to prepare the natural nail, apply a slip layer, build a balanced overlay with a correctly placed apex, create a short extension on a tip or form, and carry out infills and safe removal. Allergy prevention, hygiene, UK legislation, consultation, aftercare and honest advertising are covered throughout.
courses.delivery: Classroom course at The Looking Glass Beauty School, 4a Roushill, Shrewsbury, with pre-course study and support materials on this academy.
courses.hours_breakdown: 2.5 hours of pre-course study, 7.5 guided learning hours on the taught day, and about 7.5 hours for three post-course case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Aged 18 or over, with a Level 2 Beauty Therapy, Nail Services or equivalent qualification covering manicure, nail structure and safe salon practice. Prior gel polish experience is strongly recommended. Not open to anyone with a known acrylate or methacrylate sensitivity. Before offering the service commercially you must confirm acceptance with your own insurer.
outcomes: Explain the purpose, benefits, limitations and client suitability of builder gel, and compare it with gel polish, hard gel and liquid-and-powder acrylic.
Identify the structures of the nail unit and recognise conditions that require the service to be adapted, postponed or refused.
Conduct and record a professional consultation, obtain informed consent and create an individual treatment plan.
Explain oligomers, monomers, photoinitiators, polymerisation, lamp compatibility, under-curing and the inhibition layer.
Explain why builder gel carries a heat-spike risk that gel polish does not, and control it.
Select, handle, store and dispose of products and equipment in accordance with risk assessment, COSHH, manufacturer instructions and current UK requirements.
Prepare the natural nail without avoidable damage to the plate or living tissue.
Apply a slip layer and build a balanced overlay with a correctly placed apex, straight sidewalls and an even C-curve.
Create a short extension on a tip or form within the product's stated capability.
Infill, rebalance and remove builder gel safely by the method the product requires, and provide appropriate aftercare.

courses.title: Gel Polish Nails CPD Course
courses.short: Professional gel polish application, maintenance and removal on the natural nail. A one-day classroom course for qualified beauty and nail professionals, assessed by a theory paper, an observed practical and three case studies.
courses.description: On successful completion you will have the knowledge and practical skills to safely and confidently perform professional gel polish nail treatments. You will understand the anatomy and physiology of the natural nail and surrounding skin, carry out effective client consultations, identify contraindications and contra-actions, and maintain high standards of hygiene and health and safety. You will correctly prepare the natural nail, safely apply, cure, maintain and remove gel polish products, and give appropriate aftercare advice, with a sound understanding of the safe use, maintenance and storage of products and UV/LED curing lamps.
courses.delivery: Classroom course at The Looking Glass Beauty School, 4a Roushill, Shrewsbury, with pre-course reading and support materials on this academy.
courses.hours_breakdown: Pre-course reading and knowledge activities, 7.5 guided learning hours on the taught day, and about 6 hours for three post-course case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Aged 18 or over, with a Level 2 Beauty Therapy, Nail Services or equivalent qualification that includes manicure and pedicure knowledge, nail structure and safe salon practice. Equivalent prior learning may be accepted subject to provider and insurer approval.
outcomes: Understand the anatomy and physiology of the natural nail and surrounding skin.
Carry out an effective client consultation and identify contraindications and contra-actions.
Maintain high standards of hygiene, health and safety throughout the service.
Correctly prepare the natural nail for gel polish.
Safely apply, cure, maintain and remove gel polish products.
Understand the safe use, maintenance and storage of products and UV/LED curing lamps.
Provide appropriate aftercare advice and deliver the service to an industry standard in a safe, hygienic and commercially acceptable manner.

courses.title: Liquid and Powder Acrylic Enhancement CPD Course
courses.accredited_title: Liquid and Powder Acrylic Enhancement CPD Course
courses.short: Liquid-and-powder acrylic overlays and extensions on tips and forms. A classroom course for qualified nail professionals, assessed by a theory paper, an observed practical and post-course case studies.
courses.description: A practical course for existing nail professionals who want to offer liquid-and-powder acrylic enhancements. You will understand the chemistry of monomer liquid and polymer powder, the mix ratio and how the bead sets; prepare the natural nail; fit tips and forms; build a balanced enhancement with a correctly placed apex using the three-zone method; infill, rebalance and remove safely; and work within the health and safety controls that acrylic systems demand, including ventilation, dust extraction and allergy prevention. Consultation, UK legislation, aftercare and honest advertising are covered throughout.

courses.hours_breakdown: To be confirmed when the course is published.

Experience with gel polish or builder gel is strongly recommended. Not open to anyone with a known acrylate or methacrylate sensitivity.
outcomes: Explain the chemistry of liquid-and-powder acrylic, the mix ratio and how the product sets, and compare it with gel systems.
Identify the structures of the nail unit and recognise conditions that require the service to be adapted, postponed or refused.

Control monomer vapour, dust and skin contact in line with COSHH, the product's safety data sheet and current UK requirements.
Prepare the natural nail and fit tips and forms correctly.
Build a balanced acrylic overlay or extension with a correctly placed apex using the three-zone method.
Infill, rebalance and remove acrylic safely without damage to the natural nail, and provide appropriate aftercare.

courses.title: Electric File (E-File) Nail Technique CPD Course
courses.accredited_title: Electric File (E-File) Nail Technique CPD Course
courses.short: Safe, controlled use of an electric file on the natural nail and on the coatings and enhancements you already provide. A one-day classroom course for qualified nail professionals, assessed by a theory paper, an observed practical and three case studies.
courses.description: A practical skills course for nail professionals who already apply and remove at least one coating or enhancement system. You will learn how an electric file works (parts, speed, torque, direction, chuck and shank), which bit material, shape and grit does which job, and how speed, pressure, angle and time on one spot produce friction heat and damage and how to prevent it. Through tutor demonstration and supervised practice on cured product and on a model you will prepare the natural nail with a safety bit, reduce and remove gel polish, builder gel, hard gel and acrylic without reaching the nail plate, and shape, refine and finish an enhancement. Dust control, vibration, electrical safety, the decontamination of bits, consultation, UK legislation, aftercare and honest advertising run throughout.
courses.delivery: Classroom course at The Looking Glass Beauty School, 4a Roushill, Shrewsbury, with pre-course reading and support materials on this academy.
courses.hours_breakdown: 1.5 hours of pre-course reading, 7.5 guided learning hours on the taught day, and about 6 hours for three post-course case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Aged 18 or over, with a Level 2 Beauty Therapy, Nail Services or equivalent qualification covering manicure, nail structure and safe salon practice, and a qualification or CPD certificate in at least one of gel polish, builder gel, hard gel or liquid-and-powder acrylic with current experience of applying and removing it. The course works on those products; it does not teach them.
outcomes: Explain what an electric file is, what it can and cannot do, its benefits and limitations, and when a hand file is the right tool.
Identify the structures of the nail unit and surrounding skin, and recognise conditions that mean the electric file must not be used or the service adapted, postponed or refused.
Conduct and record a professional consultation, obtain informed consent and plan an electric-file service around the product on the nail.
Describe the parts and controls of an electric file (speed, torque, direction, chuck and shank), and set it up, check it and maintain it safely.
Select the correct bit material, shape and grit for each task, and explain how speed, pressure, angle and time on one spot produce heat and damage.
Control dust, vibration and electrical risk in line with COSHH, PUWER, the Control of Vibration at Work Regulations and manufacturer instructions, and decontaminate bits between clients.
Prepare the natural nail with the electric file: cuticle-area work with a safety bit at low speed, and de-shining without thinning the plate.
Reduce and remove gel polish, builder gel, hard gel and liquid-and-powder acrylic with the electric file, leaving a thin layer over the plate, without heat, grooves or damage.
Shape, refine and finish an enhancement with the electric file to a commercial standard.
Provide aftercare, manage contra-actions and adverse reactions, and recognise and respond to rings of fire, friction heat and an over-thinned plate.

courses.title: Lash and Brow Tint and Wax CPD Course
courses.accredited_title: Lash and Brow Tint and Wax CPD Course
courses.short: Eyelash and eyebrow tinting and eyebrow shaping by waxing, tweezing and trimming, taught as one treatment group. A one-day classroom course for qualified beauty professionals, assessed by a theory paper, an observed practical and three case studies.
courses.description: A practical skills course for beauty professionals who want to offer eyelash tinting, eyebrow tinting and eyebrow shaping safely and to a professional standard. You will revisit the anatomy of the skin, the hair and its growth cycle, the eye, the eyelids and the eyebrow, and the conditions that mean a treatment is adapted, postponed or refused; learn how an oxidative tint colours the hair, why it can sensitise and why the patch test is non-negotiable; and learn, through tutor demonstration and supervised practice on each other and on a model, to tint lashes and brows with the eyes protected and closed, and to map, wax, tweeze and trim the brows to a shape agreed with the client. Consultation, the patch-test system, hygiene, UK legislation, aftercare, emergencies and honest advertising run throughout.
courses.delivery: Classroom course at The Looking Glass Beauty School, 4a Roushill, Shrewsbury, with pre-course reading and support materials on this academy.
courses.hours_breakdown: 1.5 hours of pre-course reading, 7.5 guided learning hours on the taught day, and about 6 hours for three post-course case studies.
courses.prerequisites: Aged 18 or over, with a Level 2 Beauty Therapy or equivalent qualification covering skin structure and function, facial and eye-area treatments, consultation and safe salon practice. No previous lash or brow experience is required.
outcomes: Explain what eyelash and eyebrow tinting and eyebrow shaping are, their benefits and limitations, who they suit and when another service or a referral is the honest answer.

Describe the structure and growth cycle of the hair, the skin of the eye area and the anatomy of the eye, eyelids and eyebrow, and recognise the conditions that mean a treatment is adapted, postponed or refused.
Conduct and record a professional consultation, carry out and record a patch test, obtain informed consent and agree an individual treatment plan.

Explain how an oxidative tint colours the hair, why it can sensitise, how shade, developer and timing decide the result, and why the products are restricted to professional use and to clients aged 16 and over.
Select, handle, store and dispose of tints, developers, waxes and equipment in line with COSHH, manufacturer instructions and current UK requirements.
Prepare the client and the treatment area, protect the eyes and skin, and work hygienically throughout.
Tint eyelashes to an even, natural-looking result with the eyes protected and closed, no tint on the skin and no tint in the eye.
Tint eyebrows to a shade that suits the client, timed and checked, with the skin kept clean.
Map, wax, tweeze and trim the eyebrows to a balanced shape agreed with the client, with the wax temperature tested, the skin supported and the eyelid never waxed.
Provide aftercare, recognise and manage contra-actions, adverse reactions and tint in the eye, and set honest expectations about results and how long they last.
